brand_notes.fabric: brands.json's brand-level fabric string is 'Vinylon F canvas (waxed-canvas look) with recycled nylon waterproof lining'. Checked all six products against Fjällräven's own Material & Care accordion text and this is accurate for FOUR of six but wrong for two: (1) Hoja Top Tube Bag, Hoja Frame Bag S, Hoja Frame Bag L, Hoja Snack Bag - all four state 'Material: Vinylon F: 100% vinylal / Lining: 100% polyamide (recycled) with 10,000mm PU laminate' verbatim, and all four read as a flat matte canvas-like face in photos, consistent with Vinylon F's waxed-canvas look - the brand string is confirmed exactly for these four. (2) Hoja Handlebar Rolltop and Hoja Seatbag Drybag 16L - BOTH are pure technical dry-bags, and both state 'Material: 100% polyamide 210D Ripstop (recycled), 10,000mm PU laminate' - no Vinylon, no canvas at all. These two should be rendered as a technical ripstop dry-bag finish, not a waxed-canvas one. Net: this is a two-fabric collection (canvas-look Vinylon panel bags vs. technical ripstop rolltop drybags), and the brand string only describes the panel-bag half.
brand_notes.collab_note: I could not find any Specialized co-branding anywhere on the six product pages read (no 'Specialized' text, logo, or S-shaped mark in the product copy, descriptions, or the ~16 photos viewed) - every page is straightforwardly Fjällräven's own 'Hoja' biking sub-line, sold on fjallraven.com under Fjällräven's own name and manufacturer address. This may be correct (Fjällräven may be the sole visible brand on the actual retail product even if Specialized co-developed it, or the collab may be a different/older range), but it's worth a second look at whether 'Specialized x Fjällräven' is the right brand identity for this catalogue entry - I have not changed brands.json per the brief's rules, just flagging the mismatch between the assigned brand name and what the linked product pages actually show.
brand_notes.method: fjallraven.com sits behind a Cloudflare challenge that 403'd both a plain curl (desktop User-Agent) and WebFetch on every product URL. Per the brief, mcp__claude-in-chrome cleared it immediately - all six pages loaded normally once driven through the real browser. Each PDP uses collapsed accordions ('Product Features', 'Material And Care', 'Technical Details') that must be clicked open before get_page_text captures their content; clicking by element ref was unreliable (silently no-opped on roughly half the attempts), so I fell back to scrolling the accordion into a fixed on-screen position and clicking by pixel coordinate, which worked consistently. All six pages' Technical Details blocks give clean Height/Width/Depth/Volume figures directly from the maker - no third-party retailer sourcing was needed for this brand, unlike the 'Hoja Handlebar Rolltop' figures a previous reviewer had to reconstruct from six retailers because the live PDP wasn't accessible to them at the time.

products.name: Fjällräven Hoja Seatbag Harness + Hoja Seatbag Drybag 16L
products.dims_raw: Maker Technical Details (Hoja Seatbag Drybag 16L): Height 50cm, Width 21cm, Depth 28cm, Volume 16L, Weight 132g.
products.dims_note: TWO PRODUCTS, NOT ONE: the catalogue name bundles 'Hoja Seatbag Harness' (a separate £90 SKU - the rigid aluminium-and-webbing cradle) with 'Hoja Seatbag Drybag 16L' (a separate £55 SKU - the actual removable dry bag). Fjällräven sells them independently, same pattern as Rapha's Seat Pack in this catalogue. Dims recorded here are for the drybag alone, which is what fills the modelled volume. Maker's 'Height' (the long axis when the drybag stands upright, off the harness) maps to len once slung horizontally under the saddle - same convention used for Alpkit's Airlok Dual and Chrome's Doubletrack Saddle Roll elsewhere in this project; 'Width'/'Depth' map directly to wid/hgt. Matches the existing catalogue figures exactly.

geometry.notes: Harness-mounted drybag: a separate rigid cradle (the Hoja Seatbag Harness) clamps to the saddle rails and seatpost, and this drybag drops into and buckles onto it, wider/flatter at the nose against the harness plate and tapering toward a rounded rolltop tail - visible in the on-bike product photos.

closure.hardware: roll-top closure with an air-release valve to aid compression, per maker copy

details.seams: waterproof, roll-top sealed per maker copy
details.fabric: 100% polyamide 210D Ripstop (recycled) with 10,000mm PU laminate - NOT Vinylon, see brand_notes.fabric; matches the Handlebar Rolltop's technical drybag fabric rather than the canvas-look panel bags

mount.notes: Rigid-cradle mount via the separate Hoja Seatbag Harness (not included in this SKU) - treat like Rapha's aluminium-harness Seat Pack elsewhere in this catalogue: minimal sag, held taut by the harness rather than free-hanging fabric.
